title: People’s Mañanera August 6
author: Pedro Gellert
content:
_Every day, President Claudia Sheinbaum gives a morning presidential press
conference and Mexico Solidarity Media posts English language summaries,
translated by Mexico Solidarity’s Pedro Gellert. Previous press conference
summaries are available[here](https://mexicosolidarity.com/mananera/)._

**Science and Environment to Strengthen Energy Sovereignty  
** President Claudia Sheinbaum stated that public sector decisions are based
on scientific evidence and highlighted that the proposed measures allow for a
reduction in dependence on imported gas from the United States from 75% to
50%.

**“If there is no saltwater, there will be no exploitation of water”  
** The President reiterated that the committee recommended not using
freshwater, recycling at least 75% of the water used, protecting aquifers, and
ensuring transparency, public consultation, and environmental viability before
any project is launched.

**Audience Rights Continue in Public Consultation  
** Sheinbaum reported that a definitive proposal will be presented next week.
The President denied that the proposal represents censorship and affirmed that
“the Morning Press Conference is the most transparent exercise that can
exist.” She reiterated that media outlets should have a code of ethics and an
audience ombudsman.

**Security Strengthened to Reactivate Avocado Exports  
** The Government is working with producers in Michoacán, the Secretariat of
Foreign Relations, the Secretariat of Agriculture, and the United States to
re-establish avocado exports, following the temporary withdrawal of U.S.
inspectors. The participation of the National Service for Agrifood Health,
Safety, and Quality in inspection tasks will be evaluated.

**Infrastructure Drives Economic Growth  
** The President emphasized that the improved growth prospects for the second
half of the year are based on investments in roads, energy, water, housing,
and strategic projects. “Economic growth is not everything; what is important
is the distribution of wealth and social justice,” she stated.
